Neugebauer, co-founder and largest shareholder of Fermi Inc., disclosed that the company has dropped its lawsuit against him, which was filed to validate a 70% supermajority bylaw amendment, after a Texas Business Court ordered the company to produce documents and testimony explaining the rationale for the bylaw. Neugebauer's claims challenging the validity of the bylaw remain alive and he will continue to pursue discovery and depositions of key players. The move is seen as a significant development in the ongoing governance dispute at Fermi, with Neugebauer arguing that the board's actions were an attempt to entrench itself and avoid scrutiny.

Vishal Khanduja, Head of Broad Markets Fixed Income at Morgan Stanley Investment Management, discusses credit spreads and whether or not yields will soon peak. (Source: Bloomberg)

general.title: Apollo's Cortese Says Liquidity Is a Virtue, Not a Vice
general.summary: Apollo's Co-Head of Corporate Credit John Cortese says to expect $100 trillion in debt financing in the next decade. Cortese also says that 20% of that will be in building out AI digital infrastructure. Cortese speaks with Bloomberg's Dani Burger. (Source: Bloomberg)

general.title: Apollo’s Push for Private Credit Transparency
general.summary: Apollo is pushing to make private credit more transparent and easier to trade. The firm has now traded more than $35 billion of private credit and is putting daily valuations on an $850 billion portfolio. John Cortese, Co-Head of Corporate Credit at Apollo Asset Management, discusses the effort on Bloomberg Open Interest. (Source: Bloomberg)

general.title: Stocks, Bonds Fall on Inflation Worry as Oil Rises
general.summary: A record-breaking run in stocks hit a wall as higher oil prices lifted bond yields, stoking concerns that potential inflationary pressures could trigger Federal Reserve rate hikes. Chuck Clough, Chairman at Clough Capital, discusses what he's seeing in current markets and whether we're facing an AI bubble. (Source: Bloomberg)

general.title: Farm Machinery Shares Drop on US Probe Into Market Practices
general.summary: Shares of farm equipment manufacturers including Deere & Co. plunged after the Federal Trade Commission and the US Department of Agriculture launched an inquiry into market practices, including potential anticompetitive conduct.

general.title: AI Agent Adoption Soars on Consumer, Search Trends
general.summary: Meta's Muse has topped 6.6 million downloads since its Sept. 8 launch and reached 1.8 million daily active users, as consumers show they're ready to hand over their personal information for a chance at some AI assistance. Seema Shah, VP: Insights at Sensor Tower, discusses the growth of personal AI agents, Zuckerberg's Muse, and the broader AI market. (Source: Bloomberg)

general.summary: A studio led by the makers of the hit titles Sky: Children of the Light and Journey has raised $35 million in new funding to upend the viral “friendslop” genre of casual, whimsical video games played socially online.

general.summary: State-owned Syrian Petroleum Co. plans to more than double crude production in a year and ramp up oil refining as foreign operators return, according to Chief Executive Officer Yousef Qiblawy.

general.title: Amazon Ring Unveils $249 Smart Lock With Dial to Restore Dead Battery
general.summary: Amazon.com Inc.’s Ring brand unveiled its first smart lock, with an innovative feature that addresses the dreaded scenario of arriving home to a dead battery.

general.title: Poland Holds Rates Steady as Fuel-Price Cap Curbs Inflation
general.summary: Poland’s central bank kept interest rates on hold for a seventh month after the government cut fuel prices, easing inflationary pressures for the time being.
